ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a two-port π-type resistor network sharing the lower wire as the reference terminal. There is a 10 Ω resistor between the upper node of the left port and the lower common wire; there is a 60 Ω resistor between the upper node of the right port and the lower common wire; there is a 30 Ω series resistor between the left and right upper nodes. The port voltages are labeled V1 and V2, and the port currents are defined in the direction entering the ports. Reasoning: First write the nodal admittance equations. The current of port 1 is I1 = V1/10 + (V1 - V2)/30 = (1/10 + 1/30)V1 - (1/30)V2. The current of port 2 is I2 = V2/60 + (V2 - V1)/30 = -(1/30)V1 + (1/60 + 1/30)V2. Therefore the admittance matrix Y = [[2/15, -1/30], [-1/30, 1/20]] S. Its determinant is (2/15)(1/20) - (1/30)^2 = 1/180. The inverse matrix Z = Y^{-1} = 180 * [[1/20, 1/30], [1/30, 2/15]] = [[9, 6], [6, 24]] Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a pi-type two-port with 10 Ω left shunt, 30 Ω top series branch, and 60 Ω right shunt, all referenced to the common lower conductor. Write nodal port-current equations I1 = (1/10+1/30)V1 - (1/30)V2 and I2 = -(1/30)V1 + (1/60+1/30)V2. Thus Y = [[2/15,-1/30],[-1/30,1/20]] S. method.method_draft: First describe the image and identify the three resistors and common reference. For I2=0, looking into port 1 gives 10 Ω in parallel with (30+60) Ω, so z11=10||90=9 Ω. With V1=9I1, the current through the 30+60 branch is V1/90=I1/10, so the voltage across the 60 Ω shunt is V2=60(I1/10)=6I1, hence z21=6 Ω. For I1=0, looking into port 2 gives 60 Ω in parallel with (30+10) Ω, so z22=60||40=24 Ω. With V2=24I2, the current through the 30+10 branch is V2/40=0.6I2, so the voltage across the 10 Ω shunt is V1=10(0.6I2)=6I2, hence z12=6 Ω. Assemble Z = [[9,6],[6,24]] Ω.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The figure shows a two-port resistive network with port 1 on the left and port 2 on the right. The lower terminals 1' and 2' are connected together by a common bottom conductor, serving as the reference node. From the top node of port 1 to the reference node there is a 10 Ω vertical resistor. Between the top nodes of port 1 and port 2 there is a 30 Ω series resistor. From the top node of port 2 to the reference node there is a 60 Ω vertical resistor.

Reasoning: For z-parameters, V1 = z11 I1 + z12 I2 and V2 = z21 I1 + z22 I2. First set I2 = 0, so port 2 is open externally. Looking into port 1, the input resistance is 10 Ω in parallel with the series path 30 Ω + 60 Ω = 90 Ω. Thus z11 = 10 || 90 = (10 × 90)/(10 + 90) = 9 Ω. With V1 = 9I1, the current through the 30 Ω + 60 Ω branch is V1/90 = 9I1/90 = I1/10. The port-2 voltage is the voltage across the 60 Ω resistor, so V2 = 60(I1/10) = 6I1, giving z21 = 6 Ω.

Next set I1 = 0, so port 1 is open externally. Looking into port 2, the input resistance is 60 Ω in parallel with the series path 30 Ω + 10 Ω = 40 Ω. Thus z22 = 60 || 40 = (60 × 40)/(60 + 40) = 24 Ω. With V2 = 24I2, the current through the 30 Ω + 10 Ω branch is V2/40 = 24I2/40 = 0.6I2. The port-1 voltage is the voltage across the 10 Ω resistor, so V1 = 10(0.6I2) = 6I2, giving z12 = 6 Ω. Therefore the impedance matrix is Z = [[9, 6], [6, 24]] Ω.
